name: GitHub Copilot
note: Quota only — Copilot's sessions are read through the vscode harness. The token comes from `gh auth token` rather than an environment variable, because an app launched from Finder inherits no shell. Windows without has_quota are skipped: a free plan lists a premium tier it does not have. The endpoint is GitHub's own internal one — `copilot_internal/user` on api.github.com, which is where the OAuth token read from the CLI's host file is sent — and is published nowhere; checked 2026-09-22. Nothing here can be compared against a reference, so the fixture is the whole of the check. A window the plan reports as `unlimited` is not charted: a meter that can never move says a quota exists and that none of it has been spent, and both are false for an allowance with no cap — the same reason a balance draws its figure and no bar. Added 2026-09-24 after reading ClaudeBar's Copilot probe, which reports such a window as unlimited rather than as a percentage. The reset comes from `quota_reset_date_utc` and from nowhere else: a response that states none leaves the gauge with no countdown. Cross-read 2026-09-27 against ClaudeBar's MonthlyResetDate.swift, which computes the next 00:00 UTC on the 1st for Copilot's AI Credits — GitHub's billing cycle does roll over then, so the instant is probably right, and it is still a number the service did not send. Showing it would make a computed date indistinguishable from a reported one on the same row, which is the distinction every other figure here is careful about. The quota fixture carries a case with no reset stated, so the absence is asserted rather than assumed.

compatibility.note: Quota endpoint is runtime-validated; sessions belong to the VS Code harness.
